entries.what: `TaskTypeExample` scheduler lacks an explicit `ModifyMeta` implementation; due to `BaseScheduler` embedding/forwarding `Extension`, calling `ModifyMeta` during task modification can recurse into itself and crash.
entries.impact: If `TaskManager.ModifyTaskByID` is used with any non-`modify_concurrency` modification on `TaskTypeExample`, the scheduler can hit infinite recursion/stack overflow during `onModifying`, crashing the scheduler goroutine and potentially leaving the task stuck in `modifying` (until another owner recovers it).
entries.fix: Add an explicit no-op `ModifyMeta` to `pkg/disttask/example/scheduler.go` (and any other scheduler impl using `BaseScheduler.Extension = self`), e.g. `func (*schedulerImpl) ModifyMeta(oldMeta []byte, _ []proto.Modification) ([]byte, error) { return oldMeta, nil }`.
entries.verify: Create a `TaskTypeExample` task, call `TaskManager.ModifyTaskByID` with a non-concurrency modification (e.g. `ModifyMaxWriteSpeed`), and confirm the scheduler no longer stack-overflows and the task transitions out of `modifying` (and meta updates if implemented).
entries.evidence: `scheduler.Extension` now requires `ModifyMeta` (`pkg/disttask/framework/scheduler/interface.go:134`) and `BaseScheduler.onModifying` invokes it for any non-concurrency modifications (`pkg/disttask/framework/scheduler/scheduler.go:423`). `pkg/disttask/example/scheduler.go` sets `s.BaseScheduler.Extension = s` (`pkg/disttask/example/scheduler.go:53`) but defines no explicit `ModifyMeta` method; because `BaseScheduler` embeds the `Extension` interface (`pkg/disttask/framework/scheduler/scheduler.go:85`), the promoted forwarding method will call back into `BaseScheduler.Extension`, causing self-recursive dispatch when meta modifications are requested.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master` (f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09): `pkg/dxf/example/scheduler.go:53` still assigns `BaseScheduler.Extension = s` and still lacks `ModifyMeta`, while the interface still requires it (`pkg/dxf/framework/scheduler/interface.go:151`).
entries.summary: This commit wires non-concurrency task modifications through `scheduler.Extension.ModifyMeta` (persisting updated `task.Meta` via `ModifiedTask`) and adds new modification types for add-index app params. DDL backfill/import schedulers provide no-op `ModifyMeta`, but the Example scheduler omits an explicit `ModifyMeta`, creating a recursion/stack-overflow hazard when meta modifications are requested.

entries.subject: ddl: Implement TableMode feature (#59009)
entries.what: TableMode protection can be bypassed for `ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY` when `foreign_key_checks=0`, allowing schema changes (and possibly auto-created indexes) on tables in Import/Restore mode.
entries.impact: A session can bypass TableMode protection (Import/Restore) by setting `foreign_key_checks=0` and still mutate protected-table schema (and potentially auto-create indexes), violating the intended safety invariant during IMPORT INTO / BR restore windows and risking import/restore correctness.
entries.fix: Add an explicit mode check on the *target* table for FK DDLs (e.g. in `pkg/ddl/executor.go` `CreateForeignKey`, and ideally also in the owner/job path) so protected tables reject `ADD FOREIGN KEY` regardless of `foreign_key_checks`. Alternatively, ensure the altered table is always recorded in ResolveContext for this statement so `core.CheckTableMode` applies.
entries.verify: Put a table into `TableModeRestore`/`TableModeImport`, run `SET foreign_key_checks=0; ALTER TABLE <tbl> ADD FOREIGN KEY ...;` and confirm it returns `ErrProtectedTableMode` and does not apply FK/index metadata; also re-check the `foreign_key_checks=1` path.
entries.evidence: `ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY` sets `inCreateOrDropTable` during preprocess (`pkg/planner/core/preprocess.go:1741`), and `handleTableName` then early-returns without recording TableNameW (`pkg/planner/core/preprocess.go:1609`). The new guard only checks recorded tables (`pkg/planner/core/optimizer.go:252`), so it is skipped. The DDL path `CreateForeignKey` does not check table mode (`pkg/ddl/executor.go:5232`) and passes `ForeignKeyChecks` into the job. In the job, constraint validation is skipped when `fkCheck` is false (`pkg/ddl/foreign_key.go:672`), so no protected-table SELECT is executed to fail the job.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (f0813a3696...): `resolveAlterTableStmt` still sets `inCreateOrDropTable` for FK adds and `CreateForeignKey` still lacks a table-mode check, so the bypass remains.
entries.summary: Introduces TableMode metadata (Normal/Import/Restore), optimizer-time table-mode access checks, internal DDL ActionAlterTableMode, and exposes mode via `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES.TIDB_TABLE_MODE`.

entries.subject: ddl: reuse backend for DXF subtasks of same step (#59165)
entries.what: DXF local-sort read-index step can leak open engines on early errors: with backend reuse and `BackendCtx.Close()` no longer closing the backend, a `buildLocalStorePipeline` failure after `Register` returns without engine cleanup, leaving engines open in the shared `*local.Backend` and breaking subsequent retries/subtasks (Pebble lock/open-engine failures, potential step wedging).
entries.impact: A transient/fatal error during pipeline construction after `Register` can leave engines and Pebble DBs open in the shared backend. Subsequent retries/subtasks on the same executor may fail opening engines due to file locks, wedge the DXF add-index step, leak goroutines/FDs until step cleanup, and in worst cases risk inconsistent engine state if repeated opens were to proceed.
entries.fix: In DXF local-sort path, ensure cleanup runs on *all* error exits after engine registration when reusing a backend. Minimal fix: after `buildLocalStorePipeline` returns error, call `bCtx.FinishAndUnregisterEngines(ingest.OptCleanData)` (or at least `OptCloseEngines`) before returning. More robust: track whether `Register` succeeded and `defer` a cleanup-on-error; alternatively reset/close and recreate the shared backend on subtask failure to guarantee a clean slate for retries.
entries.verify: Inject a failure after `backendCtx.Register` / during `NewReorgCopContext` (e.g. failpoint or invalid TZ to force `time.LoadLocation` error) in DXF local-sort add-index, then observe executor retry behavior: next `RunSubtask` should be able to `Register` without Pebble lock errors, and local sort dir/engines should be cleaned (`FinishAndUnregisterEngines(OptCleanData)` runs) before retry continues.
entries.evidence: In `pkg/ddl/backfilling_read_index.go`, `(*readIndexExecutor).RunSubtask` builds a per-subtask `BackendCtx` using a shared `*local.Backend` (`Build(r.backendCfg, r.backend)`), then immediately returns on `buildLocalStorePipeline` error without any engine cleanup (`FinishAndUnregisterEngines` is only called after `executeAndClosePipeline`). `buildLocalStorePipeline` calls `backendCtx.Register(...)` before calling `NewAddIndexIngestPipeline(...)`, which can fail (it returns errors from `NewReorgCopContext`, e.g. timezone load errors via `reorgTimeZoneWithTzLoc`). With this PR, `litBackendCtx.Close()` in `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend.go` no longer closes the backend, so an early-return after `Register` leaves engines open inside the reused backend across retries/subtasks. Lightning local backend engine open is not re-entrant: `pkg/lightning/backend/local/engine_mgr.go` `openEngine()` calls `pebble.Open()` on the engine DB path and `LoadOrStore`, so a second `OpenEngine` on the same UUID before cleanup will typically hit Pebble lock errors (and/or risks duplicated ingest loops if it were to proceed).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `pingcap/master@bab4993b6f`: `pkg/ddl/backfilling_read_index.go` still returns immediately on local pipeline build error without calling `FinishAndUnregisterEngines`, and `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend.go` `litBackendCtx.Close()` still does not close the backend; no later fix found for this error-path cleanup gap.
entries.summary: Found one High issue: in DXF local-sort read-index executor, backend reuse + `BackendCtx.Close()` no longer closing the backend introduces an error-path engine leak (after `Register` but before `FinishAndUnregisterEngines`), which can wedge retries/subtasks via local engine (Pebble) reopen/lock behavior. Not fixed up to `pingcap/master@bab4993b6f`.

entries.subject: ddl: modify param at runtime for add-index on DXF local sort (#59343)
entries.what: DXF runtime concurrency modification does not update the StepExecutor’s stored `GetResource()` when applied during a running subtask. Because `readIndexStepExecutor.RunSubtask` re-reads concurrency from `GetResource().CPU.Capacity()` at each subtask start, a successful mid-subtask concurrency decrease can be lost for later subtasks, potentially rebuilding pipelines with stale (higher) concurrency and violating resource/slot assumptions.
entries.impact: After a successful runtime concurrency decrease during a running subtask, later subtasks can still start with the old (higher) `GetResource().CPU.Capacity()` value, rebuilding pipelines with oversized worker pools. This breaks the intended “runtime param modification persists” semantics and can violate the framework’s resource/slot assumptions, risking oversubscription/OOM (especially for partitioned-table add-index where an executor runs many subtasks sequentially).
entries.fix:
Prefer framework-level fix so all StepExecutors behave correctly:
- In `pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/task_executor.go` `tryModifyTaskConcurrency`, after `ResourceModified` succeeds (both increase/decrease paths), call `e.stepExec.SetResource(newResource)` (optionally before calling `ResourceModified` as well).
- Alternatively (local workaround), in `pkg/ddl/backfilling_read_index.go` `(*readIndexStepExecutor).ResourceModified`, call `r.SetResource(newResource)` after successful tuning so subsequent `RunSubtask` uses the updated resource.
entries.verify:
Manual scenario verification (no tests required):
- Run DXF local-sort add-index on a partitioned table (multiple subtasks per executor).
- While one subtask is running, issue `ADMIN ALTER DDL JOB ... THREAD = <smaller>`.
- Confirm: the currently running subtask reduces worker pool sizes; then confirm *subsequent* subtasks start with the reduced concurrency (no reversion to old higher `GetResource()` value). Add temporary logs around `pkg/ddl/backfilling_read_index.go:123` and `ResourceModified` to compare observed concurrency across subtasks.
entries.evidence:
- `pkg/ddl/backfilling_read_index.go:123` builds each subtask pipeline with `concurrency := int(r.GetResource().CPU.Capacity())`.
- `pkg/ddl/backfilling_read_index.go:204` `ResourceModified` tunes worker pools using `newResource` but never calls `r.SetResource(newResource)`.
- DXF framework applies runtime concurrency via `tryModifyTaskConcurrency` (`pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/task_executor.go:546`), which calls `e.stepExec.ResourceModified(...)` (`pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/task_executor.go:554`, `pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/task_executor.go:577`) and then records the new task concurrency via `concurrencyModifyApplied` (`pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/task_executor.go:589`) but does not update the step executor’s stored resource via `SetResource`.
- `SetResource` is only called in the between-subtask Run loop when it observes a task concurrency change (`pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/task_executor.go:296`), which won’t trigger after `concurrencyModifyApplied` has already updated `e.task`.
- `pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/manager.go:455` shows `getStepResource` returns a fresh `*proto.StepResource` each time, so the old `GetResource()` pointer cannot “self-update” to the new CPU capacity.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09`: the same pattern still exists (resource-modify path calls `ResourceModified` but does not update the stored `GetResource()` via `SetResource`; DDL step executors still read concurrency from `GetResource().CPU.Capacity()` when starting subtasks).
entries.summary: Enables runtime param modification for DXF local-sort add-index by wiring `ModifyMeta` into the backfill scheduler and adding `TaskMetaModified`/`ResourceModified` handling in the read-index step executor, plus workerpool/pipeline support for safe tuning. Found a High-severity issue: runtime concurrency/resource changes applied during a running subtask do not update the StepExecutor’s stored `GetResource()`, so later subtasks can start with stale (pre-modify) concurrency and potentially oversubscribe resources.

entries.subject: globalsort: write sorted kv meta to external storage (#59966)
entries.what: Global-sort add-index subtask meta format becomes backward-incompatible (ExternalPath + external storage), but disttask scheduling has no version/capability gating, so mixed-version clusters can dispatch these subtasks to older executors that can’t read required meta.
entries.impact: In a rolling-upgrade (or any mixed-version) cluster, global-sort add-index tasks can fail or get stuck when merge-sort/ingest subtasks land on nodes running pre-#59966 code: required subtask inputs (`DataFiles`, `MetaGroups`, `EleIDs`, range keys) are missing from the DB meta and the old executor won’t fetch the external meta, leading to runtime errors/incorrect planning and potentially requiring manual intervention/cleanup.
entries.fix:
Gate the new externalized-meta format on executor capability to avoid mixed-version breakage.
Minimal options:
- In `LitBackfillScheduler.GetEligibleInstances`, filter `eligibleNodes` to those whose `infosync.ServerInfo.Version` (or `GitHash`) is >= the first version that includes `BaseExternalMeta` + external-meta decoding, and reject/suspend the task if insufficient nodes.
- Alternatively, at task submission, verify all managed nodes are at/above the required version before allowing `CloudStorageURI`-enabled (global-sort) backfill.
- If version filtering is infeasible, keep writing legacy in-DB fields (no omission) until cluster homogeneous (but this may re-trigger the meta-size issue that motivated #59966).
entries.verify:
Repro/verification path:
1) Run a mixed-version cluster with one TiDB at this commit and one at the first-parent (pre-#59966).
2) Start ADD INDEX with global sort (CloudStorageURI configured) and ensure subtasks are scheduled across both nodes.
3) Observe old-version executor failing on merge-sort or ingest subtasks due to empty `DataFiles/MetaGroups/EleIDs` in `subtask.Meta`.
After fix, confirm scheduler excludes old nodes (or refuses task submission) and the task completes without such failures.
entries.evidence:
This commit makes global-sort add-index subtask meta backward-incompatible by externalizing fields into object storage and persisting only an `ExternalPath` pointer:
- `pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go`: `BaseExternalMeta.Marshal` returns `marshalInternalFields` when `ExternalPath != ""`, omitting any struct field tagged `external:"true"`.
- `pkg/ddl/backfilling_dist_executor.go`: `BackfillSubTaskMeta` tags `RangeJobKeys`, `RangeSplitKeys`, `DataFiles`, `StatFiles`, `MetaGroups`, `EleIDs`, and embedded `external.SortedKVMeta` as `external:"true"`; `writeExternalBackfillSubTaskMeta` sets `subtask.ExternalPath` and writes only the external fields via `WriteJSONToExternalStorage`.
- `pkg/ddl/backfilling_read_index.go` and `pkg/ddl/backfilling_merge_sort.go`: onFinished now calls `writeExternalBackfillSubTaskMeta(...)` and then stores `sm.Marshal()` back into `subtask.Meta`, meaning DB meta no longer contains `DataFiles/MetaGroups/EleIDs/...`.
Older TiDB binaries (first-parent of this commit) do not have `ExternalPath` nor any external-storage read path in `decodeBackfillSubTaskMeta`, so they will ignore `ExternalPath` and observe empty `DataFiles/MetaGroups/EleIDs`, breaking merge-sort/ingest execution.
Second confirmation (different evidence): disttask scheduling does not filter executors by version, so mixed-version clusters can dispatch these subtasks to older nodes:
- `pkg/disttask/framework/scheduler/scheduler.go`: `BaseScheduler.switch2NextStep` schedules to `eligibleNodes` derived from `NodeManager` + scope only; no use of `infosync.ServerInfo.Version/GitHash`.
- `pkg/disttask/framework/scheduler/scheduler.go:GetLiveExecIDs` enumerates all `infosync.ServerInfo` and uses `disttaskutil.GenerateExecID` (IP:PORT) with no version gating.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master`: the framework still does not version-filter executors (`pkg/dxf/framework/scheduler/scheduler.go:GetLiveExecIDs` still returns all nodes), and DDL backfill still relies on externalized meta (`pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go:BaseExternalMeta.Marshal` keeps omitting `external:"true"` fields when `ExternalPath` is set). No upstream change found that would prevent old nodes from receiving these subtasks or make old nodes able to read the external meta.
entries.summary: Commit externalizes large global-sort backfill subtask meta to object storage (meta.json) and stores only `ExternalPath` in subtask meta JSON; this risks mixed-version compatibility because older executors will ignore `ExternalPath` and see missing `DataFiles/MetaGroups/EleIDs`, while scheduling does not filter executors by version.

entries.subject: disttask: distribute merge sort subtasks to all available nodes (#60395)
entries.what: `external.DivideMergeSortDataFiles` is introduced/used to distribute merge-sort subtasks by node count, but its remainder batching can exceed the documented `MergeSortFileCountStep` cap, making its `maxTargetFilesPerSubtask := max(16, mergeConc)` overlap-budget check unsound. For some `mergeConc>16` + large-file-count inputs, this can produce merge-sort subtasks whose internal merge fanout (and thus downstream overlap/reader pressure) exceeds the intended `MergeSortOverlapThreshold` budget, risking global-sort add-index instability.
entries.impact: Under certain `(dataFilesCnt, nodeCnt, task.Concurrency)` combinations (notably `task.Concurrency>16`), merge-sort planning can generate oversized file groups that invalidate the overlap/fanout budgeting assumptions. That can lead to excessive downstream merge fanout (more target files than budgeted), increasing the chance that subsequent range-splitting/metadata iteration (which is explicitly designed around `MergeSortOverlapThreshold`) becomes unstable (resource blowups, reader limits, or planner failures), potentially stalling or failing add-index global-sort workflows.
entries.fix:
Make `DivideMergeSortDataFiles`’ sizing math consistent with its documented/assumed invariants:
- Either enforce the per-group cap for *all* returned groups (including remainder), e.g. ensure `adjustNodeCnt >= ceil(remainder/MergeSortFileCountStep)`; if that conflicts with the overlap-budget constraint, return a clear error (or proactively lower merge concurrency) instead of silently producing oversized groups.
- Or make the bound concurrency-aware by computing per-batch worst-case fanout as `max(mergeConc, ceil(batchSize/MaxMergingFilesPerThread))` and choosing `adjustNodeCnt`/batch sizes so the aggregate fanout stays under the threshold.
Also consider improving the error message (current `"unexpected zero node count"` is misleading for “cannot satisfy budget”).
entries.verify:
Add a unit test for `DivideMergeSortDataFiles` covering `mergeConc>16` with a case where `adjustNodeCnt` is reduced (like the example arithmetic), asserting:
- Every returned group size respects the intended cap (or the new cap definition).
- The aggregate fanout estimate is actually enforced: `sum(len(splitDataFiles(group, mergeConc))) <= MergeSortOverlapThreshold`.
Also add a test for “impossible” inputs to ensure a deterministic, actionable error (and no infinite retry loop behavior at the scheduler level).
entries.evidence:
DDL merge-sort planning now calls `external.DivideMergeSortDataFiles(dataFiles, nodeCnt, task.Concurrency)` when generating merge-sort subtasks (`pkg/ddl/backfilling_dist_scheduler.go:619`).

`DivideMergeSortDataFiles` documents a per-group cap of `MergeSortFileCountStep` but only enforces it for the “full rounds”; the remainder is batched via `mathutil.Divide2Batches(remainder, adjustNodeCnt)` without any `<= MergeSortFileCountStep` cap (`pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go:533`, `pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go:547`, `pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go:564`). Because `adjustNodeCnt` can be reduced by the overlap-budget loop (`pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go:557`), remainder batch sizes can exceed 4000 even though the function comment claims otherwise.

This matters because the downstream merge fanout depends on `splitDataFiles`: `shares := max(ceil(len(paths)/MaxMergingFilesPerThread), concurrency)` with `MaxMergingFilesPerThread=250` (`pkg/lightning/backend/external/merge.go:30`, `pkg/lightning/backend/external/merge.go:90`). If a returned group’s size exceeds `concurrency*250`, the number of internal merge shares (i.e. produced “target” files) can exceed `mergeConc`, breaking the `maxTargetFilesPerSubtask := max(16, mergeConc)` estimate used in `DivideMergeSortDataFiles`’ overlap-budget loop (`pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go:557`).

Concrete arithmetic example (second confirmation): with `mergeConc=20`, `nodeCnt=7`, and `fileCnt≈811999` you get `rounds*nodeCnt=196`, the loop reduces `adjustNodeCnt` to 4, and the remainder (~27999) is divided into ~7000-file batches (>4000 and >20*250). Then `splitDataFiles` yields `ceil(7000/250)=28` shares per such subtask (>20), so total target-file count can exceed the intended `MergeSortOverlapThreshold` budget even though the loop was constructed to keep it within budget.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history `HEAD..upstream/master` for `pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go`: the only related follow-up (`06674e2309`) adjusts step/threshold helpers but `upstream/master:pkg/lightning/backend/external/util.go` still batches the remainder via `Divide2Batches` without enforcing a per-group cap, so the inconsistency remains present upstream.
entries.summary: This commit changes DDL global-sort add-index merge-sort planning to split merge-sort subtasks across eligible nodes via the new `external.DivideMergeSortDataFiles`, and updates a DDL ingest memory failpoint/test. The main High-risk issue is an inconsistency in `DivideMergeSortDataFiles`: remainder groups are not actually capped by `MergeSortFileCountStep` as documented/assumed, which can break its overlap/fanout budgeting and potentially destabilize add-index global-sort planning/execution under certain concurrency + file-count combinations; this is not later-fixed on `upstream/master`.

entries.subject: ddl: Fix ddl owner doesn't use etcd keyspace prefix (#60403)
entries.what: Keyspace (API V2) rolling upgrade split-brain risk: DDL owner election keyspace prefix change makes old and new versions campaign on different etcd paths, allowing multiple concurrent DDL owners.
entries.impact: In keyspace (API V2) deployments, mixed-version rolling upgrades can create two independent DDL owner elections (legacy unprefixed vs new keyspace-prefixed). This can yield two concurrent “owners” for the same keyspace, risking concurrent DDL job execution and background owner-only tasks (e.g., dead lock cleanup), which can corrupt or stall metadata/state-machine progress.
entries.fix:
Decide/encode an explicit upgrade strategy for keyspace (API V2) deployments to avoid split-brain owners:
- Option A (safety-first): detect presence of legacy unprefixed owner keys and refuse to start (or disable DDL owner campaign) with a clear error telling operators to stop all old TiDB nodes first.
- Option B (compat window): during a deprecation window, ensure new nodes still coordinate with legacy election (e.g., take a global compat lock) so old+new cannot both act as owner simultaneously.
Also document the operational requirement for keyspace-mode upgrades.
entries.verify:
Run a mixed-version keyspace-name cluster:
- Start at least one old-version TiDB and one new-version TiDB against the same keyspace.
- Inspect etcd for both prefixes: legacy `/tidb/ddl/fg/owner/` and namespaced `/keyspaces/tidb/<id>/tidb/ddl/fg/owner/`.
- Confirm at most one effective owner is active (only one processes DDL jobs / owner-only loops) throughout the upgrade window.
entries.evidence: This commit changes the DDL owner election etcd client to be keyspace-namespaced: `pkg/ddl/owner_mgr.go:71` calls `etcd.SetEtcdCliByNamespace(cli, keyspace.MakeKeyspaceEtcdNamespace(store.GetCodec()))` before creating the owner manager (`pkg/ddl/owner_mgr.go:74`). The namespace prefix is `"/keyspaces/tidb/<keyspaceID>"` for API V2 (`pkg/keyspace/keyspace.go:36`). Keyspace mode (API V2) is enabled when `keyspaceName != ""` (`pkg/store/driver/tikv_driver.go:202`). DDL instances use `globalOwnerManager` for real-TiKV owner election when etcd is present (`pkg/ddl/ddl.go:673`). The first-parent version did not set any namespace, so it campaigned under the unprefixed `DDLOwnerKey` (`/tidb/ddl/fg/owner`).
entries.summary: Adds keyspace namespacing to the DDL owner election etcd client; this fixes cross-keyspace contention but can cause mixed-version keyspace-mode upgrades to have split-brain DDL owners due to the changed election path.

entries.subject: ddl: update row count periodically when running reorg job (#60828)
entries.what: Pause handling can leave reorg work running after a job becomes `JobStatePaused`: because reorg now returns periodic timeouts while preserving `jobCtx.stepCtx`, but the `JobStatePausing/Paused` fast-path returns without canceling that long-lived context, and the scheduler exits on paused (final state), the background reorg goroutine/workers can continue after a successful pause.
entries.impact: `ADMIN PAUSE DDL JOBS` can reach `JobStatePaused` (a scheduler final state) while the background reorg goroutine/workers keep running under the preserved `stepCtx`, continuing resource consumption and potentially continuing backfill KV work after the job is “paused”. This violates pause semantics and can leave long-lived goroutines/reorg contexts running until owner changes or the job is resumed.
entries.fix:
- When handling `JobStatePausing/Paused`, explicitly cancel/cleanup the long-lived `jobCtx.stepCtx` (and ensure cleanup isn’t skipped due to the reorg-timeout flag). A minimal approach is to cancel `stepCtx` with an `ErrPausedDDLJob` cause before returning from the pausing path, so the background reorg goroutine/workers stop before the scheduler exits on `JobStatePaused`.
- Consider mirroring the later rollback-oriented fix pattern (explicit step context cleanup when leaving running reorg), but for pause as well, so pausing reliably stops reorg resources regardless of timing.
entries.verify:
- With failpoint-enabled build: set `github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/ddl/updateProgressIntervalInMs` to a small value (< poll interval) to force frequent reorg timeouts; start an add-index reorg job; issue `ADMIN PAUSE DDL JOBS <id>`; after `ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS` reports `paused`, verify reorg/backfill work stops (row count stops increasing, no further backfill logs) and no in-memory reorg context/goroutine leak is observed.
- Add a unit/integration test that pauses immediately after a timeout return but before the next poll tick, and asserts pausing cancels the job step context and stops reorg work.
entries.evidence:
- `pkg/ddl/reorg.go`: `runReorgJob` now returns `dbterror.ErrWaitReorgTimeout` on `updateProcessTicker.C` after `job.SetRowCount(...)`/warnings merge, and sets `jobCtx.reorgTimeoutOccurred = true`, leaving the background `reorgFn()` goroutine running and keeping the `reorgCtx` in-memory.
- `pkg/ddl/job_worker.go`: `jobContext.cleanStepCtx()` skips cancelling/clearing `stepCtx` when `reorgTimeoutOccurred` is set, so `jobCtx.stepCtx` becomes long-lived across those periodic timeouts.
- `pkg/ddl/job_worker.go`: `processJobPausingRequest()` converts `JobStatePausing` -> `JobStatePaused` and returns before starting the polling goroutine (the only place that calls `jobCtx.stepCtxCancel(...)`) and without any explicit `stepCtx` cancellation.
- `pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go`: `deliveryJob` refreshes the job after every step “to handle cases like job cancel or pause”, so the step after a pause request will typically see `JobStatePausing/Paused` and take the early return path; and `model.Job.InFinalState()` treats `JobStatePaused` as final, so the scheduler stops running the job after it becomes paused—removing the last chance to cancel the still-alive `stepCtx`/reorg workers.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` (e.g. `bab4993b6f`): the reorg timeout still keeps `stepCtx` alive and `processJobPausingRequest()` still early-returns without cancel/cleanup of `stepCtx` on pausing/paused jobs, so the described pause race/behavior remains.
entries.summary: This commit changes reorg progress handling to periodically return `ErrWaitReorgTimeout` so row count/progress gets persisted to `mysql.tidb_ddl_job` during reorg, and adjusts `jobContext.stepCtx` lifecycle/polling (including multi-schema change inner-step polling suppression). One High-severity state-machine/concurrency issue remains: pausing can reach `JobStatePaused` without canceling the long-lived reorg step context, so background reorg workers may continue after the job is “paused”.

entries.subject: ddl: refresh TiFlash PlacementRules periodically (#61865)
entries.what: Periodic placement-rule “repair” can override user TiFlash replica changes due to stale job args: it submits `ActionSetTiFlashReplica` using snapshot Count/Labels, and when that job executes later it rewrites `TiFlashReplica` metadata even if a prior queued user DDL already changed/disabled TiFlash replica.
entries.impact: If a user submits `ALTER TABLE ... SET TIFLASH REPLICA ...` (disable or change count/labels) that is ahead in the DDL queue while PD rules are missing, the periodic repair job submitted later can execute afterwards and revert/override the user’s intended TiFlash replica settings, potentially re-enabling TiFlash or restoring old labels/count unexpectedly (metadata/state-machine correctness + operational surprise).
entries.fix: Avoid encoding Count/Labels from a snapshot into a delayed repair job: add a dedicated repair path/job (e.g. `ActionRepairTiFlashPlacementRules`) that, at execution time, re-reads the latest table meta and only (re)applies PD rules if `TiFlashReplica` is still enabled; do not overwrite `TiFlashReplica` Count/Labels from stale args. At minimum, include an expected (count, labels) precondition and cancel/skip if the table’s current `TiFlashReplica` differs or is nil.
entries.verify: Repro on a NextGen node: (1) enable TiFlash replica on a table; (2) delete the table/partition TiFlash placement rule in PD to make it “missing”; (3) enqueue a user `SET TIFLASH REPLICA 0` (or change labels/count) but delay its execution (e.g. with other DDLs ahead); (4) let the poller submit the repair job; (5) confirm final `SHOW CREATE TABLE`/infoschema `TiFlashReplica` reflects the user change and is not reverted after the repair job runs.
entries.evidence: `refreshTiFlashPlacementRules` builds `ActionSetTiFlashReplica` job args from the *current infoschema snapshot* (`replica.TableInfo.TiFlashReplica.Count/LocationLabels`) and submits via `doDDLJob2` (`pkg/ddl/ddl_tiflash_api.go:565`-`pkg/ddl/ddl_tiflash_api.go:637`). `doDDLJob2` enqueues then waits for completion (`pkg/ddl/executor.go:6757`-`pkg/ddl/executor.go:6764`), so the job can run after earlier queued DDLs. The job handler unconditionally rewrites `tblInfo.TiFlashReplica` from args (no guard that current settings still match) (`pkg/ddl/table.go:1083`-`pkg/ddl/table.go:1151`).
entries.summary: Adds periodic TiFlash placement-rule refresh in the DDL owner by scanning TiFlashReplica metadata and submitting `ActionSetTiFlashReplica` jobs when PD rules are missing; introduces infosync `GetPlacementRule` plumbing for TiFlash placement-rule lookup.

entries.subject: ddl: send result chunks to writers after scan task complete (#62014)
entries.what: Potential large memory spike/OOM risk: table scan now buffers all result chunks for a PD-region-sized `TableScanTask` before sending to writers, removing the prior streaming/backpressure behavior.
entries.impact: On large/wide tables with many regions and higher reorg concurrency, concurrent scan workers can retain multiple full-region scan outputs in Go heap, causing multi-GB memory spikes, long GC pauses, or OOM/crash during ADD INDEX ingest (availability and DDL stability risk).
entries.fix: Bound per-task buffering: split `TableScanTask` into smaller key ranges than a full PD region (so each task produces a small, predictable number of chunks), or add an explicit memory/row-count cap that forces re-splitting/yielding when exceeded.
entries.verify: Stress a large multi-region table (wide rows) with elevated `@@tidb_ddl_reorg_worker_cnt`, run ADD INDEX in ingest mode, and monitor TiDB heap/GC (pprof/memstats) to confirm memory stays bounded and the DDL completes without OOM/regressions.
entries.evidence: `pkg/ddl/backfilling_operators.go:550` now buffers `idxResults` (appends every fetched `*chunk.Chunk` at `pkg/ddl/backfilling_operators.go:577`) and only calls `sender(...)` after `wrapInBeginRollback(...)` completes (`pkg/ddl/backfilling_operators.go:584`). Each `TableScanTask` is a PD-region key range (`pkg/ddl/backfilling_operators.go:272`), produced via `loadTableRanges` using `BatchLoadRegionsWithKeyRange` (`pkg/ddl/backfilling.go:486`, `pkg/ddl/backfilling.go:527`). Operator wiring uses an unbuffered channel (`pkg/disttask/operator/compose.go:30`), so the previous “send-per-chunk” design applied tight backpressure; this change allows scanning to materialize an entire region’s worth of chunks in memory before any writer receives them. Reader concurrency can exceed writer concurrency based on avg row size (`pkg/ddl/backfilling_txn_executor.go:349`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (`bab4993b6fd61de478062151bb615a0e09c0aecb`): `pkg/ddl/backfilling_operators.go` still buffers per-task scan results and only sends them after the scan transaction finishes, preserving the same full-task buffering behavior.
entries.summary: Moves `TableScanOperator` to buffer per-task scan chunks and only deliver them to writers after the scan transaction finishes; adds/adjusts failpoints and a realtikv test to assert no scan transaction is in-flight during local-engine import.

entries.subject: ddl/dxf: modify ingest param at runtime for add-index with global sort (#62120)
entries.what: Runtime concurrency updates for global-sort add-index don’t reliably carry over to external-engine creation for later subtasks because `engineManager.closeEngine` uses a stale `WorkerConcurrency` copy (separate from the updated `local.Backend`), risking resource oversubscription/stalls after downscaling.
entries.impact:
After a runtime task-concurrency reduction during global-sort add-index, subsequent write&ingest subtasks on the same executor can recreate external engines with a stale higher `workerConcurrency` even though `StepResource` (CPU/mem) is already reduced. This can:
- Over-allocate memory during `readAllData`/sort (potentially blocking on the memory limiter and stalling the DDL),
- Oversubscribe CPU via `sorty.MaxGor`,
- Violate dxf/disttask resource-safety assumptions around downscaling (risking OOM or long stalls).
entries.fix:
Make worker-concurrency updates authoritative and shared for external-engine creation:
- Add a `func (b *local.Backend) SetWorkerConcurrency(int)` override that updates both `b.BackendConfig.WorkerConcurrency` and `b.engineMgr.WorkerConcurrency` (and have DDL call this), OR
- Pass an explicit concurrency into `backend.ExternalEngineConfig` and have `engineManager.closeEngine` use that instead of `em.WorkerConcurrency`, OR
- At minimum, before `CloseEngine` in `cloudImportExecutor.RunSubtask`, set backend/engineMgr worker concurrency from `e.GetResource().CPU.Capacity()` so newly created external engines match the current resource.
entries.verify:
Repro/inspection path (no tests required):
1) Run a global-sort add-index with multiple write&ingest subtasks on one executor.
2) While subtask A is running, reduce task concurrency (so `ResourceModified` applies and frees slots).
3) Observe subtask B start: confirm the newly created external engine’s `workerConcurrency` (from `engineManager.closeEngine`) matches the new concurrency, and that `LoadIngestData` does not attempt batches sized for the old concurrency under the reduced `MemCapacity`.
A minimal unit-level check would assert that after calling `backend.SetWorkerConcurrency(x)` then `CloseEngine` for an external engine, the created `external.Engine` sees `workerConcurrency==x`.
entries.evidence:
In `pkg/ddl/backfilling_import_cloud.go`, `cloudImportExecutor.ResourceModified` updates only the `*local.Backend` via `e.backend.SetWorkerConcurrency(newConcurrency)` and the currently-running `*external.Engine` via `eng.UpdateResource(...)`, but each `RunSubtask` recreates the external engine by calling `localBackend.CloseEngine(...)` again.

External engine creation for each subtask goes through `pkg/lightning/backend/local/engine_mgr.go` `(*engineManager).closeEngine`, which passes `int(em.WorkerConcurrency.Load())` into `external.NewExternalEngine(...)`. However, `pkg/lightning/backend/local/local.go` `NewBackend` copies `BackendConfig` by value into BOTH `Backend.BackendConfig` and `engineMgr.BackendConfig` (`newEngineManager(config, ...)`), so later `e.backend.SetWorkerConcurrency(...)` does not update `em.WorkerConcurrency`.

`pkg/lightning/backend/external/engine.go` uses `workerConcurrency` to (a) set `currBatchSize` in `LoadIngestData` (how many range jobs are loaded/sorted per batch) and (b) set `sorty.MaxGor = workerConcurrency*2` in `loadRangeBatchData`. Range job sizing is explicitly tied to memory-per-core (`pkg/lightning/backend/external/split.go` `CalRangeSize(memPerCore, ...)`). So if task concurrency is reduced mid-step and the next subtask recreates an external engine with the old higher `workerConcurrency`, it can oversubscribe memory/CPU relative to the new `StepResource` and undermine the framework’s “reduce resources before freeing slots to avoid OOM” contract (see `pkg/disttask/framework/taskexecutor/task_executor.go` `tryModifyTaskConcurrency`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `c49ac642..master` history and current `master` content: `pkg/lightning/backend/local/engine_mgr.go` still constructs external engines with `int(em.WorkerConcurrency.Load())`, while `pkg/lightning/backend/local/local.go` `NewBackend` still copies `BackendConfig` by value into both `Backend` and `engineManager` (no shared atomic), and there is no `(*Backend) SetWorkerConcurrency` override to propagate updates.
entries.summary: Implements disttask hooks to update global-sort add-index ingest params at runtime (write speed + ingest concurrency). A high-risk gap remains: worker-concurrency updates are not propagated to the `engineManager` copy used when recreating external engines for later subtasks, so downscaling can be silently lost and lead to stalls/OOM/CPU oversubscription.

entries.subject: ddl: add retry for updateSelfVersion (#62190)
entries.what: High risk of permanent hang / restart-safety bypass when MDL is disabled: UpdateSelfVersion now retries etcd Put “unlimited” using a non-cancelable context (via callers passing context.Background) and a lease captured once. If the etcd session/lease becomes invalid (e.g., prolonged etcd outage > TTL or domain close), the Put can never succeed and Reload can block indefinitely, preventing SyncLoop from handling syncer.Done() to stop validator and restart the syncer.
entries.impact: In MDL-disabled (classic) mode, persistent etcd/lease failures can block infoschema Reload indefinitely, freezing the schema sync loop. This can prevent processing syncer.Done (no restart) and bypass the intended schemaValidator.Stop safety gate on session loss, risking prolonged stale-schema operation (DDL propagation stalls; DML/query correctness/availability can degrade) and potentially hanging shutdown/restart flows.
entries.fix: Make UpdateSelfVersion retry bounded/cancelable and session-aware: (1) pass a cancelable ctx from SyncLoop into Reload/UpdateSelfVersion (or wrap the call with a timeout derived from lease, e.g. 2*schemaLease) instead of context.Background; (2) in etcdSyncer.UpdateSelfVersion, avoid retrying forever with a potentially-stale lease ID—break/return when s.loadSession().Done() is closed and/or re-fetch the current session lease between retries (outer retry loop that recreates OpOption each attempt).
entries.verify: Repro-style verification: in a classic/MDL-disabled run, simulate etcd outage > SessionTTL (or force session close) while a schema reload is happening and confirm SyncLoop can still hit <-syncer.Done() and restart; add a test that combines PutKVToEtcdError (forces retry) with ErrorMockSessionDone (closes session) and asserts Reload/SyncLoop doesn’t hang. Run existing realtikvtest coverage: go test ./tests/realtikvtest/ddltest -run TestUpdateSelfVersionFail.
entries.evidence: Change introduces unbounded retry on the non-MDL path: pkg/ddl/schemaver/syncer.go:289-293 now calls util.PutKVToEtcd(ctx, ..., putKeyRetryUnlimited, ..., clientv3.WithLease(s.loadSession().Lease())). Caller uses context.Background in Reload: pkg/infoschema/issyncer/syncer.go:365-408 (UpdateSelfVersion at :395) while holding s.m. PutKVToEtcd retries until ctx.Err or success: pkg/ddl/util/util.go:370-396; with context.Background it never stops. Second confirmation: Reload runs inline in the main SyncLoop goroutine (pkg/infoschema/issyncer/syncer.go:257-304), so a stuck Reload blocks handling <-syncer.Done() (and its schemaValidator.Stop()/restart safety path at :278-301). Upstream/master still has the same pattern (Reload calls UpdateSelfVersion(context.Background()), and UpdateSelfVersion uses putKeyRetryUnlimited when MDL is off), so not fixed later.
