entries.subject: ddl: skip waiting version synced without MDL for multi-schema-change (#62477)
entries.what: Compatibility/correctness risk: in non-MDL mode the restart/owner-change pre-sync is skipped when `job.LastSchemaVersion==0`; for jobs persisted by older TiDB versions (field absent => decoded as 0), this can skip required schema-version synchronization and break the online DDL 2-version invariant.
entries.impact: With `tidb_enable_metadata_lock=off`, resuming a started DDL job created by an older TiDB binary after owner crash/rolling upgrade can skip the required pre-run schema sync, violating the 2-version invariant and potentially causing online-DDL state-machine correctness issues (e.g. inconsistent DML writes/backfill gaps) if the previous owner died after committing a schema-version bump but before sync completed.
entries.fix: Preserve old behavior for “unknown” jobs: implement custom JSON unmarshal (or a decode wrapper) to detect missing `last_schema_version` and set a sentinel (e.g. `-1`), then in scheduler wait when `LastSchemaVersion != 0` (unknown or >0) and skip only when explicitly 0; alternatively, restrict the skip to `ActionMultiSchemaChange` to reduce rolling-upgrade blast radius.
entries.verify: Unit: decode a historical Job JSON blob without `last_schema_version` and ensure owner-change path still performs non-MDL pre-sync; Integration: run a DDL on an older binary with MDL off, crash owner between commit and version sync, restart with this binary, and confirm schema sync happens before the next online-DDL state transition.
entries.evidence: `pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go:562` describes maintaining the online-DDL 2-version invariant on restart/owner-change; the non-MDL pre-sync now runs only when `job.LastSchemaVersion > 0` (`pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go:583`). `Job.Decode` is plain `json.Unmarshal` (`pkg/meta/model/job.go:560`), so older job JSON without `last_schema_version` (`pkg/meta/model/job.go:397`) decodes as 0 and will skip the wait; invariant requirement is also stated in `pkg/ddl/doc.go:23`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Searched `e2e01c59d6..upstream/master` for follow-up changes and found no modifications to `LastSchemaVersion` usage; `upstream/master` still gates non-MDL pre-sync on `job.LastSchemaVersion > 0`.
entries.summary: This commit adds `Job.LastSchemaVersion` and uses it to skip `waitVersionSyncedWithoutMDL` when MDL is off and the last DDL step didn’t bump schema version; it also adds a regression test for multi-schema-change under MDL toggle. One High risk remains: jobs created by older binaries decode `LastSchemaVersion` as 0, which can incorrectly skip the restart/owner-change pre-sync in non-MDL mode and violate the online-DDL 2-version invariant; no later fix found up to `upstream/master`.

entries.subject: bootstrap: use reserved ID for system schemas/tables in nextgen (#62570)
entries.what: Nextgen bootstrap uses reserved IDs for system schemas/tables but only checks existence by ID; upgrading from an already-bootstrapped nextgen cluster with non-reserved system schema IDs can create duplicate `mysql`/`sys` schema names and cause infoschema/metadata nondeterminism.
entries.impact:
Upgrading a nextgen cluster that was bootstrapped before this change (system schemas created via DDL with non-reserved IDs) can create *duplicate* `mysql`/`sys` databases with the same names but different IDs.
This can lead to nondeterministic infoschema selection (name overwrite), system table reads/writes against the wrong schema ID, bootstrap/upgrade variables stored in an unexpected `mysql.tidb`, and hard-to-debug metadata inconsistency or startup instability.
entries.fix:
In nextgen, prevent creating a second system schema when an older/non-reserved one already exists:
- In `(*meta.Mutator).CreateMySQLDatabaseIfNotExists` (`pkg/meta/meta.go:806`), first detect an existing `mysql` DB by *name* via `GetSystemDBID()`. If found and `id != metadef.SystemDatabaseID`, return a clear error (or implement a migration) instead of creating a new reserved-ID schema.
- Do the same for `sys` in `bootstrapSchemas` (`pkg/session/bootstrap.go:1198`) before `CreateSysDatabaseByIDIfNotExists`, or enhance `CreateSysDatabaseByIDIfNotExists` to also check for name collisions and fail fast on mismatch.
- If upgrade from old nextgen clusters must be supported, add an explicit migration plan (copy+switch+cleanup) rather than silently allowing duplicate schema names.
entries.verify:
- Repro (upgrade simulation): create a store bootstrapped by pre-change nextgen (where `mysql` exists by name with a non-reserved ID), then run the new `bootstrapSessionImpl` path and confirm it does *not* introduce a second `mysql`/`sys` entry.
- Observability checks: after bootstrap, ensure `meta.ListDatabases()` contains exactly one `mysql` and one `sys` (by name), and `GetSystemDBID()` returns `metadef.SystemDatabaseID` deterministically.
- Functional check: verify bootstrap variables in `mysql.tidb` are read from the intended schema/table and infoschema has no duplicate-name overwrite.
entries.evidence:
- Nextgen startup always runs system-schema bootstrap: `pkg/session/session.go:3543-3547`.
- Bootstrap creates `mysql`/`sys` by fixed reserved IDs, only checking existence by *ID*: `pkg/session/bootstrap.go:1191-1230` calls `m.CreateSysDatabaseByIDIfNotExists`, which uses `m.IsDatabaseExist(id)` (ID-only) in `pkg/meta/meta.go:823-834`; nextgen `CreateMySQLDatabaseIfNotExists` also hardcodes `metadef.SystemDatabaseID` and calls the same helper: `pkg/meta/meta.go:806-820`.
- Meta DB creation only checks ID uniqueness, not name uniqueness: `pkg/meta/meta.go:675-692`.
- If duplicate DB names happen, the chosen `mysql` DB ID becomes order-dependent: `GetSystemDBID` scans `ListDatabases()` (`pkg/meta/meta.go:849-860`), which iterates unsorted `HGetAll` results (`pkg/meta/meta.go:1392-1407`).
- InfoSchema explicitly overwrites on duplicate schema name: `pkg/infoschema/infoschema.go:455-460`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `bab4993b6fd61de478062151bb615a0e09c0aecb`: `pkg/meta/meta.go` still hardcodes `metadef.SystemDatabaseID` for nextgen and `CreateSysDatabaseByIDIfNotExists` remains ID-only; nextgen bootstrap still calls `bootstrapSchemas` early in session bootstrap.
entries.summary: Commit switches nextgen bootstrap to create `mysql`/`sys` schemas and system tables directly via meta KV using reserved IDs tracked by a new `BootTableVersion`. Main risk: nextgen upgrades from clusters where system schemas already exist under non-reserved IDs can create duplicate schema names and lead to infoschema/metadata nondeterminism.

entries.subject: ddl,parser: modify schema to store the partial condition (#62759)
entries.what: Partial primary key condition is inconsistently handled: CREATE TABLE blocks `PRIMARY KEY(...) WHERE ...`, but ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY accepts it and then silently drops the predicate because `IndexOption.Condition` isn’t marshaled and `ConditionString` isn’t populated for PK jobs.
entries.impact: User can bypass the new CREATE TABLE restriction by using `ALTER TABLE ... ADD PRIMARY KEY(...) WHERE ...`; the `WHERE` clause is accepted but silently dropped during job args marshal/unmarshal. This creates a full primary key (or fails due to full-PK constraints) when the user requested a partial condition, and metadata/`SHOW CREATE TABLE` will not reflect the input predicate.
entries.fix:
In `(*executor).CreatePrimaryKey` (ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY path), either:
- Reject partial primary keys consistently: `if indexOption != nil && indexOption.Condition != nil { return dbterror.ErrUnsupportedAddPartialIndex... }` (matching CREATE TABLE behavior), or
- If partial PK is intended to be supported, compute `ConditionString` via `CheckAndBuildIndexConditionString` and persist it in `ModifyIndexArgs.IndexArgs[*].ConditionString` (plus worker-side restore), similar to `createIndex`.
entries.verify: Add a regression case (SQL or integration test): `create table t(a int, b int); alter table t add primary key(b) where a = 1;` should return `ErrUnsupportedAddPartialIndex` (or should persist/show the predicate if choosing to support it). Also confirm `SHOW CREATE TABLE t` behavior matches expectation.
entries.evidence:
CREATE TABLE path blocks partial PK: `pkg/ddl/create_table.go:1333`.
ALTER TABLE ADD PRIMARY KEY path does not: `pkg/ddl/executor.go:4554` builds `ModifyIndexArgs` without checking `indexOption.Condition` and without populating `IndexArg.ConditionString`.
`IndexOption.Condition` is explicitly not marshaled into DDL job args: `pkg/parser/ast/ddl.go:749` (`json:"-"`).
DDL worker restores predicate only from `arg.ConditionString`: `pkg/ddl/index.go:1095` (so PK jobs will silently lose the predicate).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (bab4993b6f...): `CreatePrimaryKey` still does not check `indexOption.Condition` or populate `ConditionString` for PK jobs, so the predicate can still be silently lost.
entries.summary: This commit adds persistence + display of partial index predicates via `model.IndexInfo.ConditionExprString` and plumbs a marshaled `IndexArg.ConditionString` for add-index jobs (surfaced in `SHOW CREATE TABLE` and `information_schema.tidb_indexes.PREDICATE`). High issue: `ALTER TABLE ... ADD PRIMARY KEY(...) WHERE ...` is still accepted but the predicate is silently lost (no `ConditionString` plumbing / no explicit rejection), allowing a bypass of the CREATE TABLE restriction and causing unexpected primary-key semantics.

entries.subject: ddl,tables: only write the index when it meets partial index condition (#62762)
entries.what: Backward-incompatible metadata/DDL-job JSON key rename for partial index condition: `IndexInfo.ConditionExprString` and `IndexArg.ConditionString` changed tag names without a decode shim, so upgrades or mixed-version clusters can silently lose the partial-index predicate.
entries.impact: Mixed-version rolling upgrade (or upgrading from builds that wrote the old keys) can silently drop the partial-index predicate from metadata/job args. That can cause nodes to disagree on whether an index is partial vs normal, change `SHOW CREATE TABLE` output, break DDL job resume semantics, and in the worst case produce wrong results/constraint behavior if an older node treats a physically-partial index as a full index.
entries.fix: Keep the original JSON tags for stable storage format, or add backward-compatible decoding: implement `UnmarshalJSON` (or a versioned wrapper) for `model.IndexInfo` and `model.IndexArg` to accept both old and new keys and marshal to a single canonical key. If upgrade compatibility is intended, also populate `IndexInfo.AffectColumn` for pre-existing partial indexes on load (or compute it lazily) so DML/DDL checks behave consistently.
entries.verify: 1) Create a table with a partial index on a binary at the first parent, persist schema to meta, restart on this commit, and confirm the predicate is preserved and enforced. 2) Reverse direction: create on this commit and restart on the first-parent binary; ensure the old binary either rejects the schema or preserves correctness. 3) Simulate rolling upgrade where an old node plans/executes queries against a partial index created by a new node.
entries.evidence: IndexInfo JSON tag for the predicate is now `condition_expr_string` in `pkg/meta/model/index.go:216` (was `partial_condition_expr_string` in the first parent). DDL job arg tag for the predicate is now `condition_string` in `pkg/meta/model/job_args.go:1374` (was `partial_condition_str` in the first parent). TableInfo is persisted/loaded via `encoding/json` in `pkg/meta/meta.go:737` and `pkg/meta/meta.go:1063`, so tag name changes directly affect on-disk schema decoding. There is no compatibility shim (no `UnmarshalJSON`, no alias field); `git grep partial_condition_expr_string` and `git grep partial_condition_str` return no matches on this commit and on `upstream/master`.
entries.later_fix_evidence: No fix found up to `upstream/master`: the old key strings don’t exist anywhere in `upstream/master`, implying no decode shim was added.
entries.summary: Reviewed commit vs first parent for DDL/add-index + metadata paths. A separate DML update inconsistency exists in this commit but is fixed later by `245c8e15f2` (PR #65808) and is therefore dropped; the remaining High issue is a backward-incompatible JSON tag rename for partial-index condition fields without any compatibility decoding.

entries.subject: table: keep `table.Columns` order by states during modifying column (#62979)
entries.what: `removingObjPrefix` rename (`_Tomestone$_` → `_Tombstone$_`) can break mixed-version / rolling-upgrade compatibility for MODIFY COLUMN tombstone name normalization when legacy-prefixed metadata exists.
entries.impact: Potential rolling-upgrade / owner-handover compatibility break for in-progress MODIFY COLUMN (especially multi-schema with multiple MODIFY COLUMN subjobs where an index can already be in “removing” name form): the new owner may fail to normalize legacy removing index names back to the correct public name, causing user-visible index names with removing prefixes, name conflicts, or DDL job failure/stuck behavior.
entries.fix: Add backward-compatible handling for the legacy prefix when stripping/recognizing removing objects: treat both `_Tomestone$_` and `_Tombstone$_` as valid removing prefixes in `getRemovingObjName`/`getRemovingObjOriginName` (and any other prefix checks), while generating new names with the corrected `_Tombstone$_` prefix.
entries.verify: Simulate a multi-schema MODIFY COLUMN where `oldIdxs[i].Name.O` is already legacy-prefixed (`_Tomestone$_...`) and ensure `markOldObjectRemoving` assigns the new/changing index the unprefixed original name and does not double-prefix the old index. Add a targeted unit test around `markOldObjectRemoving`/removing-name helpers covering both prefixes.
entries.evidence: In parent commit 6095e22d7377, `pkg/ddl/executor.go:83` defines `removingObjPrefix = "_Tomestone$_"`, but this commit changes it to `"_Tombstone$_"` (`pkg/ddl/executor.go:83`). During MODIFY COLUMN finalization, `markOldObjectRemoving` derives the *public* index name by stripping the removing prefix from `oldIdxName` (`pkg/ddl/column.go:959-972` via `getRemovingObjOriginName(oldIdxName)`), and then sets the old index name by adding the removing prefix (`getRemovingObjName(oldIdxName)`). Both helpers only recognize the *current* `removingObjPrefix` (`pkg/ddl/column.go:1444-1452`). If metadata contains legacy `_Tomestone$_...` names (e.g., from an in-flight multi-schema MODIFY COLUMN or owner handover across versions), the legacy prefix will not be stripped/recognized, producing wrong public names (still prefixed) and potentially double-prefixed tombstones.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master`: `removingObjPrefix` was refactored into `pkg/meta/model/column.go` but still uses only `_Tombstone$_`; no `_Tomestone$_` compatibility found (e.g. `git grep '_Tomestone\$_' upstream/master` is empty).
entries.summary: The commit improves MODIFY COLUMN metadata invariants by ensuring `TableInfo.Columns` remains ordered by schema states (via `moveOldColumnInfo`) and by updating `TableInfo.MoveColumnInfo` to also maintain `ChangeStateInfo.DependencyColumnOffset` across column moves, with added multi-schema test coverage. One High compatibility risk remains: renaming the internal “removing/tombstone” name prefix may break name normalization when legacy-prefixed metadata is encountered during rolling upgrade/owner handover.

entries.subject: disttask: support metering on next-gen (#63397)
entries.what: Potential nil-pointer panic on metering initialization: `InitDistTaskLoop` assumes `metering.NewMeter` never returns `nil` on success, but `NewMeter` can return `(nil, nil)` for configs with empty bucket (reachable via valid-looking URIs), and the code still starts the flush loop on `m`.
entries.impact: A non-empty but unsupported/malformed `metering-storage-uri` (e.g. `localfs:///...` or `s3:///prefix`) can trigger a nil-pointer panic in the metering flush goroutine, crashing the TiDB process and preventing DXF/next-gen DDL disttasks from running.
entries.fix: In `(*Domain).InitDistTaskLoop`, handle `m == nil` before `SetMetering`/starting the flush loop (warn + disable metering, or return a configuration error). Optionally: make `metering.NewMeter` return a non-nil error for empty/unsupported configs, and/or validate `Config.MeteringStorageURI` in `(*Config).Valid()`.
entries.verify: Run next-gen TiDB with SYSTEM keyspace DXF enabled and set `metering-storage-uri` to `localfs:///tmp/metering` (or `s3:///prefix`), then start TiDB and confirm it does not panic; expect either a clear startup error or a warning and metering disabled.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/domain/domain.go:1095-1106` parses `MeteringStorageURI`, calls `metering.NewMeter(mCfg)` and unconditionally runs `m.StartFlushLoop(do.ctx)` in a background goroutine.
`pkg/disttask/framework/metering/metering.go:137-141` returns `(nil, nil)` when `cfg.Type` or `cfg.Bucket` is empty.
`github.com/pingcap/metering_sdk/config.NewFromURI` (the function being called) supports `localfs://`/`file://` URIs which have no bucket, and also accepts cloud URIs with empty host (bucket) without error, making `m == nil` reachable.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `bab4993b6f...`: `pkg/domain/domain.go` still calls `m.StartFlushLoop(do.ctx)` without guarding `m != nil`; `pkg/dxf/framework/metering/metering.go` still returns `(nil, nil)` when `cfg.Bucket` is empty, so the crash condition still appears possible.
entries.summary: DDL add-index metering hooks are additive and the `writeChunk` KV-byte accounting fix looks correct, but DXF metering bootstrap can crash TiDB if `metering-storage-uri` parses to a config with an empty bucket because `InitDistTaskLoop` starts the flush loop on a potentially-nil `*Meter`.

entries.subject: ddl: find old column by name for old version modify column job (#63901)
entries.what: `getModifyColumnInfo` can misidentify the target column when `OldColumnID` is missing: it now looks up `_Tombstone$_<oldName>` before `<oldName>`, so tables that already contain a `_Tombstone$_<oldName>` column can cause `MODIFY COLUMN <oldName>` to operate on the wrong column.
entries.impact: If a table contains a user column named `_Tombstone$_<col>` (or a leftover internal tombstone column unrelated to the current job), `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN <col>` can pick the wrong `oldCol` on the first execution (when `OldColumnID` is still 0). This can lead to modifying the wrong column, DDL failure, or persisting inconsistent table metadata (e.g. duplicate column names) depending on the modify-column path.
entries.fix:
Disambiguate the “old column by name” fallback:
- Prefer original-name lookup for early phases (e.g. `job.SchemaState != model.StatePublic`), and only prefer removing-name lookup when the job is expected to have already renamed the old column (e.g. `job.SchemaState == model.StatePublic`).
- Additionally/alternatively, when the removing-name lookup hits, require a non-`StatePublic` column (internal removing column) before accepting it; otherwise fall back to the original-name column.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:234` now prefers `model.FindColumnInfo(..., getRemovingObjName(args.OldColumnName.L))` when `args.OldColumnID == 0`, only falling back to the original name lookup.
`pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:1124` shows new modify-column jobs don’t initialize `OldColumnID`, so the first execution always enters this name-based path.
`pkg/parser/misc.go:24` includes `$` in `isIdentChar`, so identifiers like `_Tombstone$_a` are syntactically valid (and there’s no repo-wide guard/validation for this prefix; `_Tombstone$_` only appears as `pkg/ddl/executor.go:85`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `bab4993b6fd61de478062151bb615a0e09c0aecb`: `getModifyColumnInfo` still prefers removing-name lookup first when `OldColumnID` is missing (same risk remains).
entries.summary: Commit adds a compatibility fallback for old modify-column jobs missing `OldColumnID` by searching the removing-name (`_Tombstone$_<col>`) first, plus an integration test and minor refactors (reorg-timeout helper; defaulting/logging when certain session vars are absent; a test-only job-args mutator). One High-risk edge case remains: the removing-name-first lookup can mis-target user schemas that already contain `_Tombstone$_<col>` columns.

entries.subject: modify column: support ingest/DXF mode to recreate indexes (#63970)
entries.what: Rolling-upgrade incompatibility: in-flight `MODIFY COLUMN` reorg jobs from pre-#63970 can get stuck because `AnalyzeState` moved into `job.ReorgMeta` and a new persisted `Stage` gate was introduced, but there is no migration/default handling for missing `reorg_meta.stage/analyze_state`.
entries.impact: Rolling upgrade / owner switch compatibility regression: an in-flight `ActionModifyColumn` job created by the first-parent code and already in `StateWriteReorganization` can become permanently stuck after upgrading to this commit (no reorg, no analyze, no state advancement). This can leave the table in an intermediate schema state (hidden changing column/indexes present) and require manual intervention (cancel/retry), with potential prolonged performance/behavior impact while stuck.
entries.fix:
- Add a compatibility shim so in-flight jobs from pre-#63970 can continue:
  - In `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go` (and any other modify-column reorg entrypoint), treat `job.ReorgMeta.Stage==model.ReorgStageNone` as a safe default (likely `ReorgStageModifyColumnUpdateColumn`), or infer stage from `mysql.tidb_ddl_reorg.ele_type` (column vs index element) when `Stage==0`.
  - Consider decoding legacy top-level `analyze_state` into `job.ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState` (custom decode or a deprecated alias field) so ongoing jobs don’t lose analyze progression during rolling upgrade.
- Ensure the shim is idempotent and only triggers when `Stage==0` / legacy fields present.
entries.verify:
- Repro (rolling upgrade): on the first parent (`2c25d745`), start a `MODIFY COLUMN` that requires reorg (e.g., type change with indexes) and wait until `ADMIN SHOW DDL JOBS` shows `schema_state=write reorganization`. Upgrade owner to this commit and observe whether the job continues advancing rowcount/state.
- Static check: confirm `job.ReorgMeta.Stage` can be 0 for pre-#63970 jobs (no JSON field), and that `StateWriteReorganization` path makes progress when stage/analyze are missing (after adding shim).
entries.evidence:
- `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go` (`doModifyColumnTypeWithData`, `StateWriteReorganization`): control flow is now `switch job.ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState { case None: switch job.ReorgMeta.Stage { UpdateColumn/RecreateIndex/Completed } }` with **no default / no `ReorgStageNone` handling**. If `Stage==0`, the switch does nothing and the function returns `nil`, leaving the job stuck in `StateWriteReorganization`.
- `pkg/meta/model/reorg.go`: this PR introduces `DDLReorgMeta.Stage` (with `ReorgStageNone=0`) and `DDLReorgMeta.AnalyzeState`.
- `pkg/meta/model/job.go`: this PR removes the top-level `Job.AnalyzeState` field (previously `json:"analyze_state"`), and `Job.Decode` is still a plain `json.Unmarshal` (no migration).
- First-parent behavior (pre-PR) confirms incompatibility: `2c25d745:pkg/ddl/modify_column.go` drives the reorg/analyze progression via `job.AnalyzeState` only (no stage persisted), so an in-flight modify-column job from the first parent can exist with `SchemaState=WriteReorganization` but without `reorg_meta.stage/analyze_state` fields; on this commit it deserializes as `Stage=0/AnalyzeState=0` and then no-ops forever.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Searched up to `upstream-master`: no handling of `ReorgStageNone` / `Stage==0` found (only the constant definition in `pkg/meta/model/reorg.go`), and `pkg/meta/model/job.go` `Decode` remains a plain `json.Unmarshal` without migrating legacy `analyze_state` into `reorg_meta`.
entries.summary: Adds staged modify-column reorg to allow index recreation via ingest/DXF (`ReorgMeta.Stage` + `ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState`, temp-index rollback IDs, reuse create-index backfill). Main risk found is rolling-upgrade compatibility: pre-existing modify-column jobs in `write reorganization` can deserialize with missing stage/analyze and then no-op indefinitely.

entries.subject: ddl: add timeout mechanism for add index analyze (#64096)
entries.what: `AnalyzeStateTimeout` (value 4) is persisted into DDL job metadata but first-parent code has no handler/default for this new value. During mixed-version rolling upgrades, if ownership falls back to an older TiDB while an add-index/modify-column job is between “set AnalyzeStateTimeout” and “publish/finalize”, the older owner can’t advance the state machine and the DDL job can get stuck.
entries.impact: Mixed-version rolling upgrade risk: if a newer owner writes `AnalyzeStateTimeout` (4) to an in-flight add-index/modify-column job, and ownership later moves to an older TiDB binary (pre-#64096), that older owner will not advance the job state machine. The DDL job can become stuck in `StateWriteReorganization`, potentially blocking subsequent DDLs and causing prolonged schema-change unavailability.
entries.fix:
Avoid introducing new persisted `AnalyzeState` values that older binaries can’t handle during rolling upgrade. Options:
- Encode timeout as a new JSON field (unknown fields are ignored by older versions) while keeping `AnalyzeState` in the existing set (e.g., `Skipped`), and drive `SHOW DDL JOBS` labeling from the new field.
- Or, if keeping `AnalyzeStateTimeout`, ensure timeout transitions don’t require another DDL round (finish/publish within the same round) so there’s no window where an in-queue job has `analyze_state=4` but still needs processing.
- Additionally, add a `default` branch in the analyze-state switches to treat unknown states as terminal (helps forward-compat within newer binaries).
entries.verify:
Reproduce with a mixed-version scenario:
1) On new binary, enable `tidb_enable_ddl_analyze=1` and force timeout (e.g., via failpoint/sleep as in `pkg/ddl/index_modify_test.go`). Let the job persist `analyze_state=4` while still in `StateWriteReorganization`.
2) Switch DDL ownership to an older binary (pre-#64096).
3) Observe the job no longer progresses (no matching `AnalyzeState` case), remaining in the queue indefinitely until manually intervened.
entries.evidence:
- New persisted enum value: `pkg/meta/model/reorg.go` adds `AnalyzeStateTimeout = 4`.
- New state is written mid-job: `pkg/ddl/index.go` and `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go` set `job.ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState = model.AnalyzeStateTimeout` when `analyzeTableAfterCreateIndex()` reports `timedOut`, then only publish schema in a later pass when `AnalyzeStateTimeout` is handled as a terminal state.
- First-parent code doesn’t recognize value 4 and has no default: `git show 6dc2c5b63f^:pkg/ddl/index.go` and `git show 6dc2c5b63f^:pkg/ddl/modify_column.go` inner `switch job.ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState` only covers `None/Running/Done/Skipped` (no `default`). If `AnalyzeState==4`, the switch body is skipped and the job doesn’t advance.
- This state is stored in DDL job metadata: `pkg/meta/model/reorg.go` defines `DDLReorgMeta.AnalyzeState int8 \`json:"analyze_state"\`` and `pkg/meta/model/job.go` proxies/copies `ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState` into persisted job JSON, so an older TiDB owner will read `analyze_state=4` from `mysql.tidb_ddl_job`.
entries.summary: Adds a cumulative-timeout path for the embedded post-reorg `ANALYZE TABLE` in add-index/modify-column DDL, including a new persisted `AnalyzeStateTimeout` state and logic to avoid re-running analyze across owner changes. Main High-risk concern is mixed-version compatibility: older owners can’t handle the new persisted analyze state value and may strand in-flight DDL jobs.

entries.subject: ddl: add unit test for lossy column change (#64111)
entries.what: Potential nil-pointer panic in `worker.onModifyColumn`: deferred `failpoint.InjectCall` dereferences `args` even when `GetModifyColumnArgs` returns an error (args can be `nil`).
entries.impact: If a modify-column job’s args cannot be decoded (corrupted job, version incompatibility, etc.), this turns a handled “cancel job and return error” path into a panic. The scheduler recovers panics and re-pends unfinished jobs, so this can devolve into repeated panics and a stuck DDL job instead of a clean cancellation.
entries.fix:
Move the `defer` below the `err` check, or guard it:
- After `if err != nil { ... }`, add `defer failpoint.InjectCall("getModifyColumnType", args.ModifyColumnType)`.
- Or in the deferred func: `if args != nil { failpoint.InjectCall(...) }`.
entries.verify: Add/adjust a unit test that constructs a `model.Job` for modify-column with invalid/undecodable `RawArgs` and asserts `onModifyColumn` cancels/returns error without panicking (e.g., wrap call with `require.NotPanics`). Also sanity-check that the `getModifyColumnType` InjectCall still fires for the intended test cases when args decode succeeds.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:251-258` registers `defer func(){ failpoint.InjectCall("getModifyColumnType", args.ModifyColumnType) }()` before checking `err` from `model.GetModifyColumnArgs(job)`.
`pkg/meta/model/job_args.go:62-67` returns zero `T` on decode error; for `T=*ModifyColumnArgs` (see `pkg/meta/model/job_args.go:1774-1776`) this can be `nil`, so `args.ModifyColumnType` can panic.
Parent version (`427b891^`) invoked `failpoint.InjectCall` only after successful args decode and type computation (`pkg/ddl/modify_column.go` in parent around `failpoint.InjectCall("getModifyColumnType", args.ModifyColumnType)`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master:pkg/ddl/modify_column.go` and the same `defer` before the `err` check is still present around `onModifyColumn` (i.e., not fixed later).
entries.summary: Reviewed commit diff vs first parent (DDL/modify-column + tables). Found one High issue: a new deferred failpoint hook in `onModifyColumn` can nil-deref on args decode failure, converting a clean cancel path into a panic; this is still present on `upstream/master`.

entries.subject: ddl: add checkpoint operator for DXF local add index (#64171)
entries.what: Regression in checkpoint initialization: when a checkpoint object exists but has `ts=0` (the default initial reorg_meta state), `CheckpointManager` now returns early and never allocates/persists an initial ingest TS. This undermines the intended failover/idempotency behavior around the first import and delays persisting `instance_addr`.
entries.impact:
For normal (non-DXF) local ingest add-index, the reorg table always contains a checkpoint object from initialization, so `CheckpointManager` can keep `ts=0` for a long time (until first flush/import). The first import then picks a TS inside Lightning (because `ts==0`) but that TS is not persisted in DDL checkpoint storage.
If the job/subtask fails over/crashes around the first import boundary (before the checkpoint write that would otherwise persist TS), a retry can choose a different TS for the same imported KV range, breaking the intended idempotency/failover stability and increasing risk of duplicate MVCC versions / inconsistent import semantics under retries.
Also prolongs the `instance_addr==""` “initial state” window, weakening the intended guard that local sort dir reuse is tied to the producing instance.
entries.fix:
In `CheckpointManager.resumeOrInitCheckpoint`, after applying a loaded checkpoint, if `s.ts == 0` (or `cp.TS == 0`) allocate a PD TS and persist it via `updateCheckpointImpl()` before returning. This restores the pre-existing invariant that a non-zero, persisted “next ingest TS” exists before the first import and also persists `instance_addr` early.
Alternative: make `NormalCheckpointStorage.LoadCheckpoint` treat checkpoints with `TS==0` as “not initialized” (return nil) so the existing TS-allocation branch runs.
entries.verify:
Add a unit test that inserts `mysql.tidb_ddl_reorg.reorg_meta` using the same shape as `initDDLReorgHandle` (checkpoint object present but `ts==0`), then constructs `NewCheckpointManager` and asserts:
- `GetImportTS()` becomes non-zero immediately
- storage row is updated with non-zero `ts` and non-empty `instance_addr`.
Manual/behavioral: simulate a crash after the first `SetTSBeforeImportEngine` but before checkpoint update; on resume, verify the same TS is reused (no re-import TS drift).
entries.evidence:
`pkg/ddl/ingest/checkpoint.go:492` loads cp and returns early on `cp != nil` at `pkg/ddl/ingest/checkpoint.go:498`, so the TS allocation/persist path at `pkg/ddl/ingest/checkpoint.go:527` is skipped whenever a checkpoint object exists.
Initial reorg meta inserts a checkpoint object without setting `ts`/`instance_addr` (defaults `ts=0`, `instance_addr=""`) in `pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go:779`.
Import TS is consumed for every import via `pkg/ddl/ingest/backend.go:281` -> `SetTSBeforeImportEngine`, which auto-allocates a TS when given 0 (`pkg/lightning/backend/local/local.go:1644`, `pkg/lightning/backend/local/local.go:1650`), defeating the “persist chosen TS before import/failover” intent.
Not fixed later: upstream/master still has the same early-return logic (`pkg/ddl/ingest/checkpoint.go:504` on upstream/master f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to upstream/master f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09; `pkg/ddl/ingest/checkpoint.go:504` still returns early on non-nil checkpoint without allocating/persisting TS when `ts==0`. `pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go:803` still initializes the checkpoint without TS.
entries.summary: Adds a checkpoint storage abstraction so DXF local add-index can persist checkpoints in the disttask subtask table, and wires the read-index local pipeline to use it. Main concern: in the normal (reorg-table) path, checkpoint initialization now returns early when a checkpoint object exists, so an initial `ts=0` checkpoint never gets a persisted non-zero ingest TS, weakening first-import failover/idempotency semantics.

entries.subject: ddl, model: fix unexpected missing analyze for multi schema change (#64337)
entries.what: Potential nil dereference introduced in the new multi-schema-change embedded-analyze path: `onMultiSchemaChange` now always calls `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`, which assumes `job.ReorgMeta` is non-nil, but upgrade-compat initialization only runs on reorg/background workers; MSC jobs can be dispatched to the general worker (`reorg=0`).
entries.impact: Compatibility/state-machine risk: an in-flight `ActionMultiSchemaChange` job decoded from an older TiDB version without `reorg_meta` (so `job.ReorgMeta == nil`) can panic when it reaches the new analyze gate. This is most acute when the job is dispatched to the general worker (`reorg=0`), because the existing upgrade-compat initialization does not run there. Result: DDL owner step panic / job stuck / upgrade instability.
entries.fix:
Add a nil-guard before using `job.ReorgMeta` in the new MSC analyze path, e.g.:
- Initialize in `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`: `if job.ReorgMeta == nil { job.ReorgMeta = &model.DDLReorgMeta{} }`.
- Or initialize in `onMultiSchemaChange` before calling `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`.
- Or broaden the existing upgrade-compat init in `runOneJobStep` to also cover `ActionMultiSchemaChange` even on `generalWorker`.
entries.verify:
Minimal repro (unit-level): construct a `model.Job{Type: ActionMultiSchemaChange, MultiSchemaInfo: ..., ReorgMeta: nil}` and drive it to the code path where revertible sub-jobs are done; confirm `onMultiSchemaChange` panics at `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`.
Upgrade-level: restore a job record produced by a TiDB build without `reorg_meta` into `mysql.tidb_ddl_job` with `reorg=0`, run the upgraded owner, and observe whether it hits the MSC analyze gate without crashing after applying the nil-guard.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/ddl/multi_schema_change.go:84` calls `w.doAnalyzeWithoutReorg(job, tblInfo)` unconditionally once revertible sub-jobs reach the last revertible point.
`pkg/ddl/index.go:1407` `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg` immediately dereferences `job.ReorgMeta` (`switch job.ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState`) with no nil-guard.
`pkg/ddl/job_worker.go:939` only initializes `job.ReorgMeta` on upgrade when `w.tp` is `addIdxWorker` or `backgroundWorker`.
`pkg/ddl/job_scheduler.go:419` dispatches jobs with `reorg=0` to the general worker pool.
`pkg/meta/model/job.go:772` `Job.MayNeedReorg()` can return `false` for `ActionMultiSchemaChange` (so `reorg=0` is possible).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09`: `pkg/ddl/multi_schema_change.go` still calls `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg` without a nil-guard; `pkg/ddl/index.go` still dereferences `job.ReorgMeta` in `doAnalyzeWithoutReorg`; `pkg/ddl/job_worker.go` still only initializes `ReorgMeta` for `addIdxWorker`/`backgroundWorker`.
entries.summary: Moves DDL analyze for multi-schema-change off sub-jobs (removing non-persisted `NeedAnalyze`) and into the parent MSC job using persisted `ReorgMeta.AnalyzeState`; refactors modify-column temporary naming helpers into `pkg/meta/model` and replaces `CtxVars` with `NeedReorg` for modify-column reorg signaling.

entries.subject: ddl: add auto ID rebase create table submitted by BR (#64356)
entries.what: `autoIDAccessor.CopyTo` now treats `curr==0` as “nothing to copy”, but 0 can be an explicitly stored value (not just “missing”). This can break sequence RESTART semantics across schema transfers: after `ALTER SEQUENCE ... RESTART WITH 1` (base becomes 0) and a subsequent rename back to a schema with a stale non-zero sequence value, the stale value can survive because the explicit 0 is not copied.
entries.impact: Sequences can silently lose a `RESTART WITH 1` (base=0) across a rename-back to a schema that still has a stale non-zero `sequenceKey` value: `CopyTo` skips copying the explicit 0, `Transfer` still switches allocator to the destination schema, and the destination’s stale value can be used. This violates DDL semantics and can break applications relying on sequence restart behavior; diagnosis is difficult because the rename completes successfully.
entries.fix: Change `autoIDAccessor.CopyTo` to skip only when the *source field is absent*, not when the parsed value equals 0. Use `m.txn.HGet(srcDBKey, srcField)` to distinguish `nil` (missing/deleted) from `[]byte("0")` (explicit), and `HSet` the raw bytes to the destination when non-nil. This preserves the BR cross-version safety (avoid overwriting target when source was deleted) while keeping explicit-zero semantics (notably sequence restart).
entries.verify:
SQL repro (schema names arbitrary):
1) `create database a; create database b;`
2) `create sequence a.seq start with 1 increment by 1; select nextval(a.seq);` (make prior value non-zero)
3) `rename table a.seq to b.seq;`
4) `alter sequence b.seq restart with 1;` (persists base=0)
5) `rename table b.seq to a.seq;`
6) `select nextval(a.seq);` should reflect the restart (start again), not continue from the stale pre-restart value.
entries.evidence:
`pkg/meta/meta_autoid.go:85` `autoIDAccessor.CopyTo` now does `curr := a.Get()` and returns early when `curr == 0` (`pkg/meta/meta_autoid.go:99`).
`a.Get()` uses `HGetInt64`, which returns `0` both when the field is missing and when it is explicitly stored as "0" (`pkg/structure/hash.go:85`).
Rename/apply-diff path calls `alloc.Transfer(...)` (`pkg/infoschema/builder.go:836`), which invokes `CopyTo` and then unconditionally switches allocator to the destination `(dbID, tableID)` on success (`pkg/meta/autoid/autoid.go:328`).
For sequences, `Transfer` uses the `SequenceValue()` accessor (`pkg/meta/autoid/autoid.go:1183`). `ALTER SEQUENCE ... RESTART WITH 1` persists `sequenceBase = restartValue - 1 = 0` (`pkg/ddl/sequence.go:292`, stored via `HSet` in `pkg/meta/meta.go:943`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `git log d059a7d..upstream/master -- pkg/meta/meta_autoid.go` (no follow-up changes touching this logic).
entries.summary: Adds BR-mode post-create auto ID rebasing in the DDL executor (for CreateTableWithInfo/BatchCreateTableWithInfo), adds failpoint-based tests to assert rebase call counts, and changes `AutoIDAccessor.CopyTo` to skip copying zero values to avoid overwriting downstream auto IDs during cross-version BR restore. The zero-skip in `CopyTo` appears to introduce a high-severity regression for explicitly-stored 0 values (notably sequence restart) during schema-transfer/rename paths.

entries.subject: add-index/import-into: meter row and kv size data and disable some options for import-into in nextgen (#64584)
entries.what: IMPORT INTO cleanup can become effectively non-retriable if metering send fails: `CleanUp` returns error after deleting sorted data, but still redacts `Plan.CloudStorageURI` (masking credential query params). On the next cleanup retry, the redacted CloudStorageURI may no longer authenticate to the object store, preventing cleanup from reaching metering again and leaving finished tasks stuck in active task tables.
entries.impact: If `Plan.CloudStorageURI` includes credential query parameters, a transient metering write failure can strand a succeeded IMPORT INTO task in the cleanup retry loop: task never transfers to history, cleanup may become permanently unable to access the object store (due to redaction), and row/kv-size metering may never be emitted. This can lead to persistent rows in `mysql.tidb_global_task`/`mysql.tidb_background_subtask` and repeated cleanup overhead.
entries.fix: Make cleanup retriable when metering fails: avoid redacting `Plan.CloudStorageURI` until after both file cleanup and metering succeed (don’t `defer` the CloudStorageURI redaction), or ensure retries can reconstruct the real CloudStorageURI from config/system var instead of task meta. If metering must not block GC, treat metering send as best-effort (log + proceed to `TransferTasks2History`) and add a separate retry mechanism for metering.
entries.verify: Run an IMPORT INTO where `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` (or the generated `Plan.CloudStorageURI`) contains `access-key`/`secret-access-key` params; force `handle.SendRowAndSizeMeterData`/metering writer to return an error (e.g., misconfigure metering storage or inject a metering write failure). Observe: first cleanup deletes sorted data, then fails on metering; task meta is redacted; subsequent cleanup attempts fail to access cloud storage using the redacted URI and the task stays in active task tables.
entries.evidence: `pkg/disttask/importinto/clean_up.go:59` defers `redactSensitiveInfo(task, taskMeta)` even when `CleanUp` returns an error later; after deleting sorted data, cleanup sends metering and returns the metering error (`pkg/disttask/importinto/clean_up.go:86`, `pkg/disttask/importinto/clean_up.go:91`). Redaction masks S3 credentials via `ast.RedactURL` (`pkg/disttask/importinto/scheduler.go:697`; masking behavior at `pkg/parser/ast/misc.go:3789`, especially `pkg/parser/ast/misc.go:3806`). Cleanup retries require recreating the sort store from `Plan.CloudStorageURI` (`pkg/executor/importer/import.go:1189`), but the scheduler cleanup loop keeps tasks in active tables when cleanup returns error (`pkg/disttask/framework/scheduler/scheduler_manager.go:430`). Metering errors propagate from `SendRowAndSizeMeterData` (`pkg/disttask/framework/handle/handle.go:402`).
entries.summary: Adds nextgen metering for add-index (from succeeded read-index subtask summaries) and IMPORT INTO (from post-process checksum meta) by writing row_count and KV byte sizes during scheduler cleanup; introduces `handle.SendRowAndSizeMeterData` + metering writer overwrite semantics; and disallows `checksum_table`/`record_errors` options for IMPORT INTO in nextgen.

entries.subject: ddl: sync affinity group for pd and support `show affinity` (#65049)
entries.what: `SHOW AFFINITY` bypasses database/table privilege visibility checks and can expose affinity-enabled objects (and PD topology/state) to unprivileged users.
entries.impact: Information disclosure: any user can enumerate DB/table/partition names with affinity across the cluster and observe PD affinity state (leader/voter store IDs), violating expected SHOW visibility semantics and leaking topology/metadata.
entries.fix: Add privilege filtering in `fetchShowAffinity`: for each candidate (db, table), skip DBs failing `checker.DBIsVisible(activeRoles, db)` and skip tables failing `checker.RequestVerification(activeRoles, db, table, "", mysql.AllPrivMask&(^mysql.CreateTMPTablePriv))`. Optionally require a stricter global privilege (e.g. `PROCESS`/`SUPER`) before returning PD topology fields (leader/voter store IDs).
entries.verify: Add tests creating multiple DBs/users/roles: ensure a user without DB/table privileges (or DB not visible) sees no rows for those objects via `SHOW AFFINITY`; if restricting topology fields, verify those columns are NULL/empty unless required privilege is granted.
entries.evidence: `pkg/executor/show_affinity.go:31` builds results by iterating `domain.GetDomain(e.Ctx()).InfoSchema().ListTablesWithSpecialAttribute(infoschemacontext.AffinityAttribute)` (`pkg/executor/show_affinity.go:45`) and appending rows without any visibility/privilege checks. Unlike other SHOW implementations that filter by `DBIsVisible` + `RequestVerification` (e.g. `pkg/executor/show.go:443`, `pkg/executor/show.go:570`), `SHOW AFFINITY` has no calls to `privilege.GetPrivilegeManager`. Planner also adds no `visitInfo` for `ast.ShowAffinity` (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:3630`). Later history: no commits touch `pkg/executor/show_affinity.go` up to `upstream/master` (`git log a14f0c8..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/show_affinity.go` is empty).
entries.later_fix_evidence: No later changes up to `upstream/master`: `git log a14f0c8..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/show_affinity.go` returns empty.
entries.summary: This commit implements PD affinity-group lifecycle sync during DDL (create/alter/truncate/drop/database drop) and adds `SHOW AFFINITY`. One remaining High issue: the new `SHOW AFFINITY` path lists affinity tables across all schemas and exposes PD affinity state without any DB/table visibility or privilege filtering.

entries.subject: ddl: support region split policy (#65133)
entries.what: Persistent region split policy accepts arbitrarily large `REGIONS` values (no `SplitRegionMaxNum` cap), enabling unbounded split-key generation and potential DoS/stability issues.
entries.impact: A user with DDL privileges can bypass the existing `SplitRegionMaxNum` safety limit by using the new persistent split policy syntax (CREATE/ALTER TABLE ... SPLIT ... REGIONS N). With a large enough `(upper-lower)` range, this can drive unbounded key generation (`O(N)` allocations/CPU) and huge split requests, potentially causing severe memory pressure/OOM, long stalls, or cluster instability (and it may happen asynchronously when `tidb_scatter_region` is off).
entries.fix: Enforce an upper bound for `splitOpt.SplitOpt.Num` in `normalizeSplitPolicy` using `config.GetGlobalConfig().SplitRegionMaxNum` (same as `SPLIT REGION` statements). Consider a defensive runtime guard in `applySplitPoliciesForTable` as well (reject or clamp) to protect against corrupted metadata.
entries.verify: Add/extend integration tests to assert `CREATE TABLE ... /*T![region_split]*/ SPLIT ... REGIONS <SplitRegionMaxNum+1>` and `ALTER TABLE ... SPLIT ... REGIONS <SplitRegionMaxNum+1>` fail with a clear error, and that values at/below the limit still succeed (both table-level and index-level policies). Also validate that large-but-valid ranges do not trigger excessive key generation after the fix.
entries.evidence: `pkg/ddl/split_region.go:365` only rejects `REGIONS < 1` in `normalizeSplitPolicy` and does not enforce the existing `SplitRegionMaxNum` cap; the resulting `policy.Regions` is later used directly to generate split keys via `regionsplit.GetSplitTableKeys(..., int(policy.Regions), ...)` and `regionsplit.GetSplitIndexKeys(..., int(policy.Regions), ...)` (`pkg/ddl/split_region.go:259`, `pkg/ddl/split_region.go:309`). Key generation ultimately loops `num-1` times and allocates per iteration in `util.GetValuesList` (`pkg/util/split.go:24`, `pkg/util/split.go:30`). By contrast, the existing `SPLIT TABLE/INDEX ... REGIONS` statement path enforces `SplitRegionMaxNum` in the planner (`pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5178`, `pkg/planner/core/planbuilder.go:5276`).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `f0813a369666ac6314e76f5e573e982fe50c8a09`: `pkg/ddl/split_region.go` still contains no `SplitRegionMaxNum` enforcement for `normalizeSplitPolicy` (`git show upstream/master:pkg/ddl/split_region.go | rg SplitRegionMaxNum` returns nothing). No intervening commits touched the relevant files (`git log 35d50f2b..upstream/master -- pkg/ddl/split_region.go` is empty).
entries.summary: Reviewed diff vs first parent for ddl/meta changes introducing persistent region split policies (`TableInfo.TableSplitPolicy`, `IndexInfo.RegionSplitPolicy`) and a new DDL action (`ActionAlterTableSetRegionSplitPolicy`) that applies policies during pre-split/scatter. Found one High-severity issue: the new normalization path lacks the existing `SplitRegionMaxNum` upper bound, allowing extremely large `REGIONS` values to trigger unbounded key generation and potentially destabilize TiDB/cluster.

entries.subject: table: Non-clustered table non-unique global index needs partid in key, v1 (#65380)
entries.what: Mixed-version/downgrade incompatibility: `GlobalIndexVersionV1` changes global non-distinct index key format by inserting `PartitionIDFlag`+partitionID into the key, but there is no compatibility gating to prevent creating these v1 indexes when older TiDB binaries may still be serving traffic. Older binaries would ignore the new metadata field and also cannot decode the new key suffix flag (126), risking query/index correctness during rolling upgrades or after downgrade.
entries.impact: Rolling upgrade / mixed-version cluster risk: if a v1 global index is created while any TiDB nodes still run the pre-v1 code, those nodes can’t decode non-distinct global index keys (flag 126 in key suffix) and will mis-handle index access (query errors or wrong results) and/or index maintenance (writes using legacy key format won’t match v1 keys). Downgrade risk: older versions will not understand v1 keys but will still see the index as `Global` and attempt to use it.
entries.fix: Add an explicit mixed-version compatibility gate before producing `GlobalIndexVersionV1` indexes. Options: (1) refuse CREATE/ADD GLOBAL INDEX that would require v1 unless all TiDB instances report a version that supports v1 (similar pattern exists in `pkg/ddl/ddl.go:1019` for job version gating); or (2) force legacy v0 format with a warning (but then the original collision bug remains). If downgrade is supported, also add downgrade protection/documentation (v1 indexes should block downgrade or require rebuild).
entries.verify: Design-level: add a unit/integration test that simulates `infosync.GetAllServerInfo` returning at least one “old” TiDB version and assert DDL rejects (or forces legacy) when creating a global index that would need v1. Runtime-level: in a real rolling-upgrade test (old+new TiDB), run the PR’s reproduction (EXCHANGE PARTITION creating duplicate `_tidb_rowid`, then create global non-unique index) and ensure old nodes either (a) never observe v1 indexes (DDL refused), or (b) can still query correctly (if backward-compat decoding is implemented).
entries.evidence: This commit introduces a new metadata field `IndexInfo.GlobalIndexVersion` (new in `pkg/meta/model/index.go:256`), sets it to `GlobalIndexVersionV1` for certain new global indexes (`pkg/ddl/index.go:354`), and changes non-distinct index key encoding to prefix the handle suffix with `PartitionIDFlag`+partitionID when `GlobalIndexVersion>=V1` (`pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go:1259`). In the first-parent code, `decodeHandleInIndexKey` did not recognize `PartitionIDFlag` and immediately calls `codec.DecodeOne` on the key suffix; `codec.DecodeOne` errors on unknown flags (`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:1312`), so a v1 key starting with 126 would fail decoding. Because older binaries would also ignore the new JSON field, they would treat the index as legacy while encountering v1 keys on disk, causing read/write incompatibility in mixed-version scenarios.
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `f0813a3696`: `pkg/ddl/index.go` still sets `GlobalIndexVersionV1` without any cluster-version gate, and `pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go` still encodes `PartitionIDFlag` into keys for v1; no follow-up compatibility guard was found via `git log 2f9776e8..upstream/master -- pkg/ddl/index.go pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go pkg/meta/model/index.go`.
entries.summary: Adds `GlobalIndexVersion` to global index metadata and introduces v1 global index key encoding that includes partition ID in the key for non-clustered non-distinct global indexes (and unique-with-NULL cases) to prevent key collisions after EXCHANGE PARTITION; updates DDL backfill/DML key generation accordingly and adds tests. Main risk: lacks mixed-version/downgrade compatibility gating for the new on-disk key format.

entries.subject: importinto: introduce a param to control conflict resolution (#66701)
entries.what: `Plan.GetOnDupKeyMode()` defaults missing (legacy) task metadata to `error`, which changes conflict handling for IMPORT INTO DXF tasks created before this option existed (legacy capture → now error) when those tasks are resumed after upgrade.
entries.impact: **Compatibility/metadata correctness:** IMPORT INTO disttask metadata generated before this PR won’t contain `Plan.OnDupKey`. After upgrade/resume, those tasks will implicitly switch from legacy “capture conflicts” to “error on conflict”, causing unexpected job failure on duplicate keys (and potentially leaving partially-processed import state requiring manual recovery).
entries.fix:
Preserve legacy semantics for pre-option task metadata:
- Change `(*Plan).GetOnDupKeyMode()` default for empty to `OnDupKeyModeCapture` (legacy behavior) OR introduce an explicit task-meta/version field and map “missing OnDupKey” -> capture only for legacy tasks.
- Keep new default for newly-created plans by continuing to set `p.OnDupKey = OnDupKeyModeError` in `initDefaultOptions` (already done).
entries.verify:
- Add a regression test that unmarshals legacy `TaskMeta` JSON without `on_dup_key` and asserts the executor path uses capture-mode `onDup` (or at least `Plan.GetOnDupKeyMode()` returns capture for empty).
- (Optional) Simulate an in-flight task upgrade: create a task meta blob from pre-change code, run merge/ingest step selection, and assert it doesn’t fail solely due to missing `OnDupKey`.
entries.evidence:
- Legacy behavior (first parent): `git show 97edb43^:pkg/dxf/importinto/task_executor.go` shows `getOnDupForKVGroup()` returned `engineapi.OnDuplicateKeyRecord` for `external.DataKVGroup` and `getOnDupForIndex()` returned `OnDuplicateKeyRecord` for unique indexes unconditionally (capture-style conflict handling).
- New behavior: DDL task execution now derives `onDup` from task metadata via `m.taskMeta.Plan.GetOnDupKeyMode()` in `pkg/dxf/importinto/task_executor.go:443-447`, and `Plan.GetOnDupKeyMode()` treats empty as error in `pkg/executor/importer/import.go:337-346` (explicitly noting old task metadata has empty).
entries.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (at `f0813a3696`): `git log 97edb43..upstream/master -- pkg/executor/importer/import.go` shows no follow-up changing `GetOnDupKeyMode`, and `upstream/master:pkg/executor/importer/import.go` still returns `OnDupKeyModeError` when empty.
entries.summary: Found one High-severity compatibility issue: legacy IMPORT INTO DXF tasks (metadata created before `on_duplicate_key`) will default to `error` on resume due to `GetOnDupKeyMode()` treating empty as error, changing prior capture semantics and potentially breaking in-flight jobs after upgrade. No later fix observed up to `upstream/master`.
